issues.failure_explanation: The proof only shows upper bounds for the clean and outlier gradient sums and then writes the outlier sum as the minimum of those upper bounds. Equality of the norms and upper bounds do not imply the required inequality εG ≤ (1-ε)L||w_sgd-w*||; in particular no lower bound on the outlier (or clean) gradient norm is established. issues.failure_explanation: The step replacing \sum_{i∈O}p_i(wsm) by ε^k is not justified. For MKL, ε^k is not an upper bound on the probability that the selected minimum-loss sample is an outlier; with replacement, if outliers have the lowest losses the total outlier selection probability can be 1-(1-ε)^k, which is large as k grows. The proof also evaluates G at w_sgd rather than w_sm and conflates the local strong-convexity constant m with the global λ.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair for the unconditional lemma identified; at minimum, a repair must bound the total outlier probability at wsm by a valid expression or add an explicit hypothesis such as \sum_{i∈O}p_i(wsm)≤ε^k.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that any MKL stationary point satisfies ||w_sm-w*||≤ε^kG/λ is unsupported; Theorem relativebounds and the appendix lemma m2lbound, which use the same ε^k bound, are affected.
issues.title: MKL stationary-point bound unjustifiably uses ε^k as outlier probability
issues.why_classification: The core worst-case robust bound changes substantially if valid sampling probabilities are used; the source does not support a local fix preserving the unconditional claim.

The main R_t omits this term, so the displayed inequality is too strong for noisy good samples. A simple no-outlier two-quadratic example with nonzero individual gradients at w* violates the claimed bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose the iteration $\bs{w_t}$ satisfies that $f_{i}(\bs{w_t})<f_{j}(\bs{w_t})$ for $i \in \mathcal{G}, j \in \mathbb{O} $.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary statement permits the best good loss to equal the worst outlier loss, but the proof and the rank-based probabilities require the good samples to be strictly the first |G| samples in loss order. With ties, the selected-sample probabilities are not fixed by the ordering, so the proof does not cover the stated boundary case.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the rest of the paper, we will focus on the ``with replacement'' scenario for ease of presentation; this choice does not change our main ideas or results.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces the minimum of the coefficients (n-2i+1)/(n(n-1)), i≤|G|, by |G|/(n(n-1)). The true minimum is (n-2|G|+1)/(n(n-1)), which is smaller whenever |G|>(n+1)/3; this range is allowed by |G|≤n/2. The same proof also uses the without-replacement k=2 probability formula, whereas the paper's main analysis uses with-replacement sampling, so the residual bound is not established for the stated MKL-SGD algorithm.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the residual with the correct probability model and use the true minimum coefficient (n-2|G|+1)/(n(n-1)), strengthening the noise-level conditions accordingly; or restrict the corollary to |G|≤(n+1)/3 and specify the sampling model.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's claim that R_t^{(MKL_2)}≤R_t^{(SGD)} under the given noise-level conditions is unsupported for a significant part of the advertised regime and for the with-replacement algorithm used in the paper.
issues.title: Corollary overestimates extra contraction coefficient and uses inconsistent sampling
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained but requires reoptimizing constants or weakening the regime; it does not need new global architecture but loses some of the advertised >half-corruption claim.
